blocks.text: Fruittari or Fruittarit (for groups) is a fashion movement and a subculture that emerged in Finland during the mid-2000s to early 2010s, with a term defining teenage boys who pay close attention and take pride in their appearance. The "Fruittari" originated from the term "Fruitcake", which is translated in Finnish. Alongside contemporary spaces such as Hopparit (Hip-hop ties) or Pissikset (A girl version), they shared groups online through social platforms like IRC-Galleria.

The main components of the style incorporate tight skinny jeans, distinct layered hairstyles, branded hoodies, and accessories like large-buckled belts, defying narrow and traditional 2000s masculine norms similar to the Gyaruo, Scene, and Partille-Johnny aesthetic.

The major components of the style featured specific 2000s streetwear brands like Svea beanies, WESC hoodies, Paul Frank t-shirts, Kone Helsinki belts, Lacoste shoes with massive buckles, often white, and tight-fitting skinny jeans that were a staple of the signature look. For the hair, it was styled into a large, bold, side-swept fringe and avoluminous pouf colloquially related to as a "bird's nest" (linnunpesä).

The term was used derogatorily as a homophobic insult to mock teenage boys who spent time, money on self-expression and grooming while they proudly reclaimed the term as a memorable marker of the mid-2000s nordic subculture.
